To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the activity of cytochrome P-450 (P450), a key enzyme in the metabolism of xenobiotics, decreases in fatty liver; (b) this effect is mimicked in an in vitro model in which hepatocytes accumulate lipids by incubation with long-chain free fatty acid mixtures; and (c) this effect is not related to the decrease of P450 gene expression but is probably due to the inhibition of P450 by lipids.
the accumulation of lipid droplets in the cytoplasm of hepatocytes is associated with decreased activity and mRNA levels of P450 enzymes.

the accumulation of lipids induced by FFA treatment of cultured human hepatocytes leads to a significant decrease in P450 activities and mRNA expression levels, and that this effect may explain the reduction of P450 enzymes in fatty livers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an in vitro model for studying the effect of steatosis on human hepatic drug-metabolism enzymes.
the potential impact of steatosis on the P450 enzymes of human hepatocytes isolated form liver grafts discarded for liver transplantation.
the use of human hepatocytes isolated and cultured from discarded fatty liver grafts for in vitro studies on drug metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of human hepatocyte cultures from fatty liver for in vitro metabolic studies should be carefully evaluated and, in some cases, may be considered.

the impact of steatosis on P450 activities is not a major concern, and that the reduction in P450 activities observed in fatty liver is mainly due to the reduced number of hepatocytes present in the tissue.
fatty liver grafts are not suitable for clinical transplantation but could be used as a source of human hepatocyte for in vitro drug metabolism studies and for other therapeutic applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human hepatocytes from steatotic livers are metabolically active but that the P450 enzymes are reduced in number and/or function.

fatty liver grafts are a valuable source of functional human hepatocytes for pharmacotoxicological studies and that hepatocyte cultures exposed in vitro to FFA can be used to investigate the impact of steatosis on drug metabolism.

the presence of lipid droplets in the liver is associated with decreased P450 activities and that this effect is not due to a direct inhibition by the lipid accumulation, but rather to an indirect effect on the P450 gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of hepatocytes from fatty livers for in vitro studies is not recommended.
the in vitro model of cellular steatosis can be useful to study the effect of lipid accumulation on P450 enzymes.
the presence of lipid accumulation in the cytosolic compartment may be a critical factor that affects P450 activities in human hepatocytes.
